name: Client Hints (Accept-CH, Critical-CH)
plain: Servers ask the browser for extra device details through request headers.
meaning: A server sends Accept-CH to receive hints such as Sec-CH-UA-Platform-Version, Arch, Bitness, Model, Device-Memory, DPR and Viewport-Width. Critical-CH forces a retry with them. Chromium only; Firefox and Safari do not send them.

web.api: Accept-CH and Critical-CH response headers; Sec-CH-* request headers

steps: Browser adds hints on later requests

limits.headline: Can ask your browser for extra device details such as model, OS version and screen
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a page loads and the site asks for hints
can: Ask for details such as platform version, device model, memory and screen width
Tailor images and pages to your device
Make your browser retry the request with those details on sites that require them
cannot: Get these details from Firefox or Safari, which do not send them
Get details the browser does not offer; it sends only what the site asks for
Know who you are from them alone
limits.differs: Only Chromium browsers (Chrome, Edge, Samsung Internet) send them. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: The server can ask your browser for extra details about your device with each request.

marketing.name: User-Agent Client Hints
marketing.pitch: Chrome pitches it as a more private, structured replacement for the old user agent string, where sites ask for the details they need.

story.for_you: You never see it. When a site asks, your browser quietly sends things like your device model, system version, screen density and memory size. The site then sends the right image size or layout.
story.for_makers: Makers use hints to send the right images, files and layout for each device, which makes pages faster. Fraud and ad systems also use the detail as a fingerprint input, so what a server asks for matters.

use_cases.example: A browser game site picks the right graphics quality and download size for a weak phone or a strong gaming laptop.
A cloud gaming site reads device and screen details to choose the stream resolution and controls.
A streaming site picks video quality and app layout for your TV, phone or laptop.
A store sends smaller images to a low memory phone so the page loads fast.
An ad system reads device model and system version to match ads to phone models.
A fraud tool checks that hints agree with the browser claim, and a mismatch reveals a spoofed device.
A product team counts visitors by exact device model and system version.

technical_bounds: High entropy hints only sent after server opt-in and to first party by default

value.abuse: Gets precise OS and device model without JS

history.change: UA Client Hints on by default
